mainTopic: The four special שבתות (שקלים, זכור, פרה, החדש): how they are read and which שבת each one falls on
overview: This amud deals with the four special שבתות before פסח: שקלים, זכור, פרה, and החדש. It opens by finishing the debate about how to read שקלים when the weekly פרשה is next to it. רבי יצחק נפחא has the seventh reader simply continue into שקלים, while אביי has him go back and repeat it so it stands out. A ברייתא saying 'read it and repeat it' first seems to help אביי, but the גמרא explains that 'repeat' can mean reading it on two separate שבתות. When שקלים falls on כי תשא itself, אביי's plan of reading the whole פרשה and then repeating שקלים is supported by a ברייתא. Next, רב and שמואל argue about when ראש חודש אדר, or פורים, falls on Friday: רב moves שקלים or זכור to the earlier שבת, and שמואל pushes it to the next day. Each proof brought for רב is pushed away, and their dispute is matched to an older dispute between תנאים. The גמרא then defines the third שבת, פרה, and ends with a ברייתא listing all four readings with their הפטרות.

steps.title: People will think the reading just continued and stopped there
steps.stepSummary: This line ends the challenge to רבי יצחק נפחא. If the seventh person simply reads on from תצוה into שקלים, people will think it is the normal weekly reading that went a bit longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: People will say: they just extended the reading and stopped there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its challenge to רבי יצחק נפחא's plan. If the seventh person just reads on into שקלים, nobody will notice it was a special reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יצחק נפחא's plan, פרשת שקלים flows straight on from the weekly reading with no break. The problem is that the public will not see it as a separate reading for שקלים. They will think the reader just went further than usual and then stopped. The whole purpose of reading שקלים is to announce the half-shekel, so it must be clearly noticed.

keyTerms.meaning: Stopping, setting the end point of the reading

phrases.english: People will say: it is just stopping
phrases.notes: What onlookers will mistakenly think

phrases.english: that they are stopping there.
phrases.notes: They will see it as the end of a longer weekly reading, not as a separate שקלים reading

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אוֹקוֹמֵי הוּא דְּקָא מוֹקְמִי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge (from the previous part of the daf) against רבי יצחק נפחא's way of reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's plan: the seventh person simply reads on from תצוה into שקלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reading that flows straight on is not noticed as a separate reading, so the public misses that שקלים was read at all

steps.title: אביי's plan: read through, then repeat שקלים
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the six readers cover from תצוה all the way to 'וְעָשִׂיתָ', which already includes שקלים. Then the seventh goes back and reads שקלים again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: six people read from 'וְאַתָּה תְּצַוֶּה' until 'וְעָשִׂיתָ'. Then one person goes back and reads again from 'כִּי תִשָּׂא' until 'וְעָשִׂיתָ'.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the problem just raised, אביי gives a new plan. The seventh reader goes back and repeats the שקלים section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the weekly readers cover all the text, including the שקלים section. The seventh person deliberately goes back to 'כִּי תִשָּׂא'. Because it is a repeat, everyone notices it is a special reading for שקלים. This fixes the exact problem from Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier view and brings a new one)
Opening words of פרשת שקלים, the start of פרשת כי תשא
'And you shall make' a copper כיור, the end point of the שקלים section
Repeats and reads (reads the same section a second time)

steps.confusionAlert: 'עַד וְעָשִׂיתָ' means up to but NOT including 'וְעָשִׂיתָ כִּיּוֹר'. Both the six readers and the seventh reader stop at the same spot, so the seventh is clearly a repeat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea that repeating a section makes it stand out as a special reading.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
phrases.notes: Brings a new plan instead of רבי יצחק נפחא's

phrases.english: six people read from "And you shall command"
phrases.notes: The start of the weekly פרשה, תצוה

phrases.english: until "And you shall make" (the copper laver),
phrases.notes: This goes past the end of תצוה and through the שקלים section

phrases.english: and one person repeats and reads
phrases.notes: The seventh reader

phrases.english: from "When you take the count" until "And you shall make."
phrases.notes: The שקלים section, read a second time

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new plan that solves the problem raised in Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six people read from תצוה through the end of the שקלים section, and the seventh repeats the שקלים section from 'כִּי תִשָּׂא' to 'וְעָשִׂיתָ'

steps.title: A ברייתא says we read שקלים and repeat it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. When the weekly פרשה is right next to שקלים, whether just before it or just after it, we read שקלים and repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If it falls on the פרשה next to it, whether before it or after it, we read it and repeat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to test the two opinions. This step quotes the source; the next step will spell out whom it helps and whom it hurts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא deals with exactly our case: the weekly reading is right next to שקלים. Its ruling is 'קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ וְכוֹפְלִין אוֹתָהּ', meaning we read it and read it again. A repeat matches אביי's plan, not רבי יצחק נפחא's plan, where שקלים is read only once.

keyTerms.meaning: Right next to it (the next-door פרשה)
And they repeat (read it a second time)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: Opens a challenge from a ברייתא

phrases.english: If it falls on the portion adjacent to it,
phrases.notes: The שבת of שקלים falls when the weekly reading is right next to the שקלים section

phrases.english: whether before it or after it —
phrases.notes: 'Before it' is תצוה, the פרשה just before שקלים; 'after it' is ויקהל, just after. The כי תשא case itself comes later, in Steps 7–10.

phrases.english: they read it and repeat it.
phrases.notes: Notice the word 'repeat'; that's the key point here.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: חָל לִהְיוֹת בַּפָּרָשָׁה הַסְּמוּכָה לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier source that tests אביי's plan against רבי יצחק נפחא's
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's plan, where שקלים is read only once
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls for a repeat ('כופלין'), which רבי יצחק נפחא's plan does not include

steps.title: The ברייתא fits אביי but is hard for רבי יצחק נפחא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the result. The ברייתא fits אביי well, but it is a difficulty for רבי יצחק נפחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to אביי this works well. But according to רבי יצחק נפחא, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states clearly whom the ברייתא hurts. It supports אביי and challenges רבי יצחק נפחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בִּשְׁלָמָא' sets up a contrast: this fits one side, but not the other. The word 'וְכוֹפְלִין' in the ברייתא matches אביי's repeat. Since רבי יצחק נפחא never repeats שקלים, the ברייתא is now a real difficulty for him, and an answer is expected next.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (sets up a contrast)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two plans for שקלים when it is next to the weekly פרשה. In רבי יצחק נפחא's plan, the seventh person just continues into שקלים. In אביי's plan, the seventh person repeats שקלים so it stands out. At first, the ברייתא's word 'וְכוֹפְלִין' seems to support אביי, but Steps 5–6 show that it does not decide the question.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Abaye it works out well,
phrases.notes: אביי's plan reads the שקלים section twice, which fits the word 'וְכוֹפְלִין', 'repeat'.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa it is difficult!
phrases.notes: רבי יצחק נפחא's plan never reads it twice.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַבָּיֵי נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the result of the ברייתא quoted in Step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires repeating שקלים, which only אביי's plan does

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא turns the question back on אביי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא answers that the ברייתא does not fit אביי either. The 'before' case works, but the 'after' case can never happen in אביי's way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא could answer you: Does the ברייתא really fit אביי? The 'before' case is fine. But the 'after' case, how could that ever happen?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא defends himself by showing that אביי has a problem with the same ברייתא. This sets up the next step, which reinterprets the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of שקלים falling either 'before' or 'after' the weekly פרשה that contains it. Under אביי's reading, 'repeating' means reading שקלים twice on the same day, and that fits the 'before' case. The 'after' case can never happen that way, since כי תשא is never read before ראש חודש אדר. So אביי cannot read the ברייתא literally either.

keyTerms.meaning: And does it work well for אביי? (turning the challenge back on the other side)
It works out fine (for this part)
Before it / after it (the weekly פרשה of שקלים)
How can you find such a case? (it never happens)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha could say to you:
And for Abaye, does it work out well?
It is fine for 'before it',
phrases.notes: When the שבת of שקלים comes right before the weekly reading of כי תשא.

phrases.english: but 'after it', how can you find such a case?
phrases.notes: This can never happen, so the ברייתא cannot mean reading twice on one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא: וּלְאַבָּיֵי מִי נִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יצחק נפחא against the difficulty in Step 4 by showing that אביי's reading of the ברייתא also fails.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's understanding of the ברייתא (repeating שקלים on the same day)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's 'after it' case can never happen under a same-day repetition, so אביי cannot read the ברייתא literally either.

steps.title: Repeating means reading it on two different weeks
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's 'repeat' must mean reading שקלים on two separate שבתות. That applies to both cases, so the ברייתא is no proof against רבי יצחק נפחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? 'Repeat it' means on two different שבתות. Here too, it means repeating it on two different שבתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יצחק נפחא's defense. It explains the ברייתא's word 'repeat' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Repeat' means reading שקלים once as the special reading and again as part of the regular weekly פרשה on a different שבת. Once we read it this way, the ברייתא says nothing about reading twice on the same day. So the difficulty against רבי יצחק נפחא falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must you say? (you are forced to explain it this way)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'repeat שקלים' means reading it on two separate שבתות. So it does not decide between רבי יצחק נפחא and אביי.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Repeat' here does NOT mean twice on the same day. It means once as the special reading and once as the regular weekly reading, on two different weeks.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
One repeats it on (separate) Shabbatot,
phrases.notes: This explains the 'after it' case.

phrases.english: here too, one repeats it on (separate) Shabbatot.
phrases.notes: The same explanation applies to the 'before it' case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the defense begun in Step 5 by giving the correct meaning of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'repeat' meant reading שקלים twice on the same day, which would support אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Repeat' means reading it on two separate שבתות, so the ברייתא does not argue with רבי יצחק נפחא.

steps.title: When שקלים falls on the שבת of כי תשא itself
steps.stepSummary: New case: the special שבת of שקלים is the same שבת as כי תשא. רבי יצחק נפחא says six read from 'וְעָשִׂיתָ' to 'וַיַּקְהֵל', and the seventh reads שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it falls on the שבת of כי תשא itself, רבי יצחק נפחא said: Six people read from 'וְעָשִׂיתָ' until 'וַיַּקְהֵל'. Then one person reads from 'כִּי תִשָּׂא' until 'וְעָשִׂיתָ'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case, where the special reading and the weekly פרשה start at the same place. רבי יצחק נפחא gives his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening section of כי תשא is itself the שקלים reading. So רבי יצחק נפחא skips it in the regular reading and starts the six readers after it, at 'וְעָשִׂיתָ'. The seventh then reads the opening section as שקלים, so nothing is read twice.

phrases.english: If it falls on 'Ki Tisa' itself,
phrases.notes: The שבת of שקלים is the same שבת as the weekly פרשה of כי תשא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:
Six read from 'And you shall make' until 'And he assembled',
phrases.notes: This is the rest of כי תשא, without its opening section.

phrases.english: and one reads from 'When you take' until 'And you shall make'.
phrases.notes: The seventh reads the opening section, which is the שקלים reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל לִהְיוֹת בְּ״כִי תִשָּׂא״ עַצְמָהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of שקלים falling next to כי תשא to the case where it falls on כי תשא itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six read the rest of כי תשא, from 'וְעָשִׂיתָ' to 'וַיַּקְהֵל'. The seventh then reads the opening section as שקלים.

steps.title: אביי objects: it looks like reading backwards
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that people will think the Torah is being read out of order.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged it: Now people will say that he is reading backwards!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבי יצחק נפחא's ruling for this new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seventh reader goes back to the start of כי תשא, after the others have already read later sections. People will not realize this is the special שקלים reading. They will think the weekly פרשה is being read out of order, which is not allowed.

phrases.english: Abaye objected to it:
Now people will say
that he is reading backwards!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק נפחא's ruling in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's order of reading when שקלים falls on כי תשא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ending with an earlier section makes it look like the weekly פרשה was read out of order.

steps.title: אביי's ruling: read the whole פרשה, then repeat שקלים
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that six read all of כי תשא until 'וַיַּקְהֵל', and then the seventh repeats the שקלים section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Six people read until 'וַיַּקְהֵל'. Then one person repeats and reads from 'כִּי תִשָּׂא' until 'וְעָשִׂיתָ'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his own ruling to replace רבי יצחק נפחא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weekly פרשה is now read fully and in order, including its opening. When the seventh goes back to the opening, it is clearly a second reading for שקלים, not an out-of-order weekly reading. This matches אביי's earlier approach of repeating שקלים on the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, he said (giving a replacement ruling)
Repeats and reads (reads it a second time)

steps.whatToRemember: When שקלים falls on כי תשא itself, אביי rules that six read the whole פרשה. The seventh then repeats the שקלים section, so no one thinks the Torah is being read out of order.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the concern that the congregation must clearly see the difference between the weekly reading and the special reading.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Six read until 'And he assembled',
phrases.notes: They read all of כי תשא, including its opening section.

phrases.english: and one repeats and reads
from 'When you take' until 'And you shall make'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יצחק נפחא's ruling after the objection in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six read all of כי תשא until 'וַיַּקְהֵל', and the seventh repeats from 'כִּי תִשָּׂא' to 'וְעָשִׂיתָ' as שקלים.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when שקלים falls on the שבת of כי תשא, the section is read and then repeated. This matches אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא, like אביי: If the שבת of שקלים falls on the שבת of כי תשא itself, we read the section and then read it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up אביי's ruling from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the six readers read all of כי תשא in order, and then the seventh repeats the שקלים section. The ברייתא says the same thing: 'read it, and repeat it.' This supports אביי against רבי יצחק נפחא, who split the reading so that the section was not read twice.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him (a support)
The weekly פרשה that opens with the מחצית השקל
We repeat (read it a second time)

steps.whatToRemember: The final word on the כי תשא case: read the פרשה in order, then repeat the שקלים section. This is אביי's view, and a ברייתא supports it.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Abaye:
If it falls on 'Ki Tisa' itself,
they read it and then repeat it.
phrases.notes: First as part of the regular weekly reading, then again as שקלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's ruling from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that the שקלים section is read twice on שבת כי תשא

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a ראש חודש in the middle of the week
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. If ראש חודש אדר falls in the middle of the week, שקלים is read on the שבת before.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If ראש חודש אדר falls in the middle of the week, we move the reading earlier, to the שבת that has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This line sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that שקלים is read on the שבת on or before ראש חודש אדר. So if ראש חודש falls on a weekday, we read it on the שבת before. The open question is what to do when ראש חודש falls on Friday, right before שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שבת' means 'the week,' not the day of rest. 'בתוך השבת' means 'in the middle of the week.'

phrases.english: If it falls during the week,
they advance it to the Shabbat that passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ראש חודש אדר falls on a weekday, שקלים is read on the שבת before it.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about a ראש חודש on Friday
steps.stepSummary: When ראש חודש אדר falls on Friday, רב says we read on the earlier שבת. שמואל says we read on the next day, שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If ראש חודש אדר falls on Friday, רב said: we move the reading earlier. שמואל said: we push it later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between אמוראים about the borderline case of Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Friday is technically 'in the middle of the week,' so it may seem to fit the משנה's rule. But the very next day is שבת. רב moves the reading back a full week. שמואל waits until the next day.

phrases.english: It was stated: The New Moon of Adar
that falls on Friday:
Rav said: They advance it (to the previous Shabbat);
and Shmuel said: They defer it (to the following day).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's rule to the borderline case of Friday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב says read on the earlier שבת. שמואל says read on the following שבת.

steps.title: רב's reason: there must be enough days before the tables
steps.stepSummary: רב reads early so that there will be enough days between the announcement and the setting up of the money tables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to move it earlier because otherwise there would be too few days before the tables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב rules that we read on the earlier שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money-changers' tables (שולחנות) were set up on ט״ו אדר to collect the שקלים. The announcement needs two full weeks before that. If ראש חודש is Friday and we read on שבת (the 2nd), then the 15th falls only 13 days later. That is too short, so רב reads on the earlier שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The money-changers' tables set up on ט״ו אדר to collect the שקלים

phrases.english: Rav said they advance it,
because if so (if they read the next day), there would be too few
days before the tables.
phrases.notes: There would be less than two weeks before the 15th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading on the later שבת would leave less than two weeks before the tables, so רב reads earlier.

steps.title: שמואל's reason: the tables will not go out until Sunday
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers רב's concern. In such a year, the 15th falls on Friday, and the tables will not go out until Sunday. So two weeks will still pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to push it later. He would tell you: In the end, the 15th falls on Friday, and the tables do not go out until Sunday. So we push it later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains שמואל's view by showing how he answers רב's worry about the count of days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ראש חודש is Friday, then the 15th is also a Friday. The tables would not be set up on a Friday, only on the Sunday after. From reading on שבת the 2nd until Sunday the 17th is a full two weeks, so there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (gives the other side's reply)
Sunday (the first day of the week)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said they defer it;
he could say to you: Ultimately,
the fifteenth falls on Friday,

phrases.aramaic: וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹת לָא נָפְקִי עַד חַד בְּשַׁבָּא,
phrases.english: and the tables do not go out until Sunday;
therefore they defer it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's reason from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A calendar fact shows the concern does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reading on שבת the 2nd would leave only 13 days before the tables on the 15th.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tables do not go out on Friday the 15th, only on Sunday the 17th, so a full two weeks still pass.

steps.title: Trying to prove רב from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that when ראש חודש falls during the week, we read on the earlier שבת. The גמרא suggests this includes Friday, which would support רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If it falls during the week, we move it to the earlier שבת, and we skip a later שבת. Doesn't this include even Friday?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove רב's view from the plain wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'during the week' without any limit. The גמרא suggests this covers every weekday, including Friday. If so, the משנה is saying to read early even when ראש חודש is on Friday, which is exactly רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: We skip, take a break (from the special readings)
Is it not? (introduces a suggested proof)

phrases.english: We learned: If it falls during the week,
they advance it to the past (Shabbat),
and they skip on the following Shabbat.
Is it not referring even to Friday?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the dispute by using the משנה to support רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a Friday ראש חודש means reading on the earlier שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'חל להיות בתוך השבת מקדימין לשעבר'

steps.title: The משנה means only the true middle of the week
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה refers only to the middle of the week, not to Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means specifically the middle of the week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב by reading the משנה more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בתוך השבת' can mean the actual middle of the week, not Friday. Read this way, the משנה does not discuss Friday at all. So it gives no proof for רב, and שמואל's view still stands.

phrases.english: No; it means specifically during (the middle of) the week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only this proof is rejected. The dispute itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'בתוך השבת' includes Friday. It may mean only the true middle of the week.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to prove רב's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the first special שבת is the one whose week contains ראש חודש אדר, even when it falls on Friday. The גמרא reads this as proof that we read early even in the Friday case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Which is the first שבת? It is the שבת of any week in which ראש חודש אדר falls, even if it falls on Friday. Doesn't this mean that the Friday case is like a midweek case? Just as in a midweek case we read early, so too when it falls on Friday we read early!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof for רב, this time from a ברייתא. The ברייתא seems to put the Friday case in the same group as the midweek case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the משנה in Step 15 was rejected in Step 16, because the משנה might mean only the middle of the week. This ברייתא says Friday outright: 'even on Friday.' If Friday is treated like the midweek days, then we move the reading to the שבת before, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Within it, meaning during that week
The day before שבת, meaning Friday
Isn't it that...? The גמרא's way of offering an inference as a proof

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Which is the first Shabbat?
Any one in which the New Moon of Adar falls
to be within it (within its week),
and even on Friday.
Is it not that 'even on Friday'
is similar to 'within it' (midweek)?
phrases.notes: The Friday case is put in the same group as the midweek case.

phrases.english: Just as midweek, we read early,
so too on Friday, we read early!
phrases.notes: This supports רב.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵיזוֹ הִיא שַׁבָּת רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected, a new proof is brought from a ברייתא that names Friday outright.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that when ראש חודש אדר falls on Friday, we read on the earlier שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא defining the first שבת as the one whose week contains ראש חודש אדר, 'even on Friday.'

steps.title: שמואל changes the wording of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the ברייתא should read 'on it' (בָּהּ) instead of 'within it.' The school of שמואל had the same version.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The text should say 'on it.' And so the school of שמואל taught: 'on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes away the proof by giving a different wording of the ברייתא. His own school taught the ברייתא with that wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the word 'on it,' the first שבת is the שבת on which ראש חודש itself falls. It is not the שבת of the week that contains ראש חודש. Read this way, 'even on Friday' means that when ראש חודש falls on Friday, we read on the next day, which is שבת. That matches שמואל's view instead of רב's.

keyTerms.meaning: On it, meaning on that שבת itself
The school of שמואל taught: a ברייתא as it was learned in שמואל's study hall

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל is just guessing at a new text. He supports the word 'on it' with the ברייתא as his school learned it. So this is a real second version of the text, not an invented fix.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: 'On it.'
phrases.notes: שמואל reads the wording as 'on it' (בָּהּ) instead of 'within it' (בְּתוֹכָהּ).

phrases.english: And so the school of Shmuel taught: 'On it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 17 by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא is removed, because the ברייתא now supports שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depended on the wording 'within it.' The correct version is 'on it.'

steps.title: The dispute matches an older dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב and שמואל match a dispute in a ברייתא. רבי יהודה הנשיא says there can be a break between the special שבתות, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says there is no break.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of the תנאים: 'We skip a שבת between the special readings,' said רבי יהודה הנשיא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: 'We do not skip.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב and שמואל are repeating an older dispute between two תנאים. This step brings the two opinions, and the next step explains them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Skipping' means that on one שבת in the middle, no special portion is read. That happens if we read שקלים early, in שבט. רבי יהודה הנשיא allows a skip, which fits רב's early reading. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says there is no skip, at least in the Friday case, which fits שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the תנאים: this argument of אמוראים matches an older argument of תנאים
We skip, leaving a gap between the special שבתות

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of tanna'im:
'We skip among the Shabbatot,'
phrases.notes: One שבת goes by with no special portion.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
We do not skip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs and rejections, the גמרא places the argument between רב and שמואל on top of an older argument between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה הנשיא allows a gap between the special שבתות. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not allow one.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר limits his view to the Friday case
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains that he says 'no skipping' only when ראש חודש falls on Friday. When it falls midweek, even he agrees that we read early, in שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: When do I say we do not skip? When ראש חודש falls on Friday. But when it falls in the middle of the week, one reads early on the שבת before, even though it is still שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains exactly when his rule applies. This makes it clear that the תנאים argue about the same Friday case as רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Friday case, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads on the next day, so the four portions come on four weeks in a row. That is שמואל's view. In the midweek case, everyone reads early in שבט. So רבי יהודה הנשיא, who allows a skip even on Friday, must hold like רב.

keyTerms.meaning: When? Used here to set the limit of a ruling
The שבת that passed, meaning the previous שבת

steps.whatToRemember: רב matches רבי יהודה הנשיא: on Friday, read early and there is a skip. שמואל matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: on Friday, read the next day and there is no skip. In the midweek case, everyone reads early.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב and שמואל are not inventing a new argument. Each one follows the view of a תנא, so neither can be easily pushed away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
When do I say that we do not skip?
When it falls on Friday,
phrases.notes: Then he reads on the next day, so the weeks run in a row.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹךְ הַשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: but when it falls in the middle of the week,
one reads early on the previous Shabbat,
even though it is still Shevat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: אֵימָתַי אֲנִי אוֹמֵר אֵין מְסָרְגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר from Step 19 and limits it to the Friday case. This completes the match with רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no skip only when ראש חודש אדר falls on Friday. When it falls midweek, we read early in שבט.

steps.title: New dispute: פרשת זכור when פורים falls on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's next line about פרשת זכור. It brings a dispute: when פורים falls on Friday, רב says to read זכור early, and שמואל says to read it later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'On the second שבת, we read זכור.' It was stated: When פורים falls on Friday, רב said: We read פרשת זכור early. שמואל said: We read it later.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and brings a new argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרשת זכור, about עמלק, should be read before פורים, because המן came from עמלק. When פורים falls on Friday, רב reads זכור on the שבת before פורים. שמואל reads it on the שבת right after, the day after פורים. This follows the same pattern as their argument about ראש חודש on Friday.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion about remembering what עמלק did

phrases.english: 'On the second, Zakhor,' etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: It was stated:
When Purim falls on Friday,
Rav said: We read the portion of Zakhor early,
phrases.notes: On the שבת before פורים.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: We read it later.
phrases.notes: On the שבת right after פורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁנִיָּיה זָכוֹר וְכוּ׳. אִיתְּמַר: פּוּרִים שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: פרשת זכור, instead of פרשת שקלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When פורים falls on Friday, רב reads זכור on the שבת before, and שמואל reads it on the שבת after.

steps.title: רב's reason: remember before you celebrate
steps.stepSummary: רב says we read זכור early, on the שבת before פורים, so that the doing of פורים does not come before the remembering of עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: we read it early, so that the doing (celebrating פורים) does not come before the remembering (reading זכור).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the reason behind רב's opinion from the last step. רב wants זכור read before פורים, never after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading פרשת זכור is the 'remembering' of עמלק. Celebrating פורים is the 'doing.' The order should be remembering first and doing second, so if פורים is on Friday, זכור must be moved back to the שבת before.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing: the actual celebration of פורים
Remembering: the reading of פרשת זכור

steps.whyThisMatters: The ideas of 'doing' and 'remembering' are what this whole debate turns on. שמואל's answer in the next step uses the same two words.

phrases.english: Rav said: we move it earlier —
phrases.notes: זכור is read on the שבת before פורים.

phrases.english: so that it should not come first,
the doing before the remembering.
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in אסתר that says the days are 'remembered and done' (נזכרים ונעשים), with remembering listed first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב's ruling, which was stated without a reason in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When פורים falls on Friday, זכור is read the שבת before, so remembering comes before doing.

steps.title: שמואל's reason: in walled cities they come together anyway
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says we read זכור later. He answers רב's concern: walled cities celebrate פורים on the fifteenth, which is that שבת, so for them remembering and doing fall on the same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: we push it later. He would tell you: since there are walled cities that celebrate on the fifteenth, the doing and the remembering come together at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's reason and shows how he would answer רב's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פורים is Friday the 14th, then שבת is the 15th. That is the day walled cities (מוקפין) celebrate שושן פורים. So in those cities, the reading of זכור and the doing of פורים happen together. שמואל holds that this is good enough, and nobody does the doing before the remembering.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (how he answers the other side)
Walled cities, which celebrate פורים on the 15th

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not ignore the idea of remembering before doing. He agrees with it. He just says that 'together' is acceptable, and it happens on that שבת in the walled cities.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: we push it later —
phrases.notes: זכור is read on the שבת after Friday's פורים.

phrases.english: he would say to you:
phrases.notes: This introduces שמואל's answer to רב's reason.

phrases.english: since there are walled cities
that celebrate on the fifteenth,
phrases.notes: That is the שבת itself.

phrases.english: the doing and the remembering
come together at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reason and answers רב's argument directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When פורים falls on Friday, זכור is read the following שבת, because in walled cities the doing and the remembering then fall on the same day.

steps.title: Proof for רב from the משנה's 'second שבת'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says זכור is read on the 'second' שבת. If ראש חודש אדר is on שבת, פורים is on Friday, and the second שבת is before פורים. That seems to support רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: on the second שבת we read 'זכור.' But when ראש חודש falls on שבת, פורים falls on Friday, and still the משנה teaches: on the second שבת, 'זכור'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove רב's view from the plain words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Count it out: ראש חודש on שבת means שבת is the 1st (שקלים), the 8th, and so on, and the 14th (פורים) is Friday. The 'second' שבת is the 8th, which comes before פורים. The משנה makes no exception for this case, so it seems זכור is read early, as רב says.

keyTerms.meaning: ראש חודש, the first of the month

phrases.english: We learned: on the second, 'Zachor.'
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי מִיקְּלַע רֵישׁ יַרְחָא בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: But when the New Moon falls on Shabbat,
Purim falls on Friday,
phrases.notes: The 14th is a Friday.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches: on the second, 'Zachor'!
phrases.notes: The second שבת is the 8th, before פורים, as רב says.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both reasons are given, the גמרא looks for a source that decides the dispute in favor of רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that זכור is read early when פורים is on Friday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'on the second שבת, זכור,' read in the case where ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'second' means second after the break
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא pushes off the proof. 'Second' means the second שבת with a special reading, counted after a שבת with no reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: what does 'second' mean? Second, after the break.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the proof by reading the word 'second' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל can count only the שבתות on which a special portion is read. In this case the 8th has no special reading, so it is a break. The next reading, on the 15th, is still called the 'second.' So the משנה fits שמואל too, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A break: a שבת with no special reading

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
What does 'second' mean?
Second, after the break.
phrases.notes: The second reading, which comes after a שבת that was skipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה is rejected. רב's view itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'second' means the second שבת of the month. It can also mean the second שבת with a special reading.

steps.title: Proof for רב from a ברייתא: 'even on Friday'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the second שבת is the one whose week contains פורים, 'even if פורים is on Friday.' The גמרא reads Friday as being like midweek, so we read early, as רב says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: which is the second שבת? Any week that פורים falls within, even on Friday. Doesn't this mean Friday is like 'within the week'? Just as within the week we read early, so on Friday we read early!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof for רב, this time from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא groups Friday together with the middle of the week. When פורים is midweek, everyone agrees זכור is read on the שבת before. So Friday should be treated the same way, and that is רב's view. This argument works exactly like the one about שקלים in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it mean...? (the start of a proof)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Which is the second Shabbat?
Any week in which Purim falls,
and even on Friday.
Doesn't it mean:
Friday is like 'within the week';
just as within the week we read early,
so too on Friday we read early!
phrases.notes: This is רב's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was pushed off, the גמרא tries a new proof from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that זכור is read early when פורים is on Friday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: 'any week that פורים falls within, even on Friday.'

steps.title: שמואל corrects the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the ברייתא should read 'on it' (on the שבת itself), not 'within it.' The school of שמואל taught it that way too.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: read 'on it.' And so the school of שמואל taught: 'on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes off the proof by changing one word in the ברייתא, just as he did with the שקלים ברייתא in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the reading 'on it,' the ברייתא means the second שבת is the one on which פורים falls, or the one right after פורים. So 'even on Friday' supports reading later, not earlier. The school of שמואל had this version in their own text, which backs up the correction.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמואל taught (their version of the ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs for רב were pushed off: the משנה by reading 'second' as 'after the break,' and the ברייתא by reading 'on it' instead of 'within it.' The dispute between רב and שמואל still stands.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: 'on it.'
phrases.notes: שמואל reads it as 'on it' instead of בתוכה, 'within it.'

phrases.english: And so the school of Shmuel taught: 'on it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא in step 26, using the same kind of correction as in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא is rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depends on the word 'within it.' The correct text is 'on it,' so Friday is not grouped with midweek.

steps.title: פורים on שבת itself: everyone agrees, no early reading
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that when פורים falls on שבת itself, even רב agrees we read זכור on that שבת and do not move it earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: If פורים falls on שבת itself, רב הונא said: According to everyone, we do not move the reading earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at a new case: פורים falls exactly on שבת. רב הונא says that here רב and שמואל both agree that זכור is read on that same שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the argument was about פורים falling on Friday. רב wanted remembering (זכור) to come before doing (פורים). When פורים is on שבת itself, the remembering and the doing fall on the very same day, so רב הונא holds that רב has no reason to move זכור earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת itself (the actual day of שבת)
according to everyone (here, both רב and שמואל)
we do not move it earlier

phrases.english: If it (פורים) occurs on Shabbat itself,
phrases.notes: A new case, different from פורים on Friday.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
According to everyone, we do not read it early.
phrases.notes: Even רב agrees in this case.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת עַצְמָהּ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the Friday case to a new case, פורים on שבת, and limits the רב/שמואל dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When פורים falls on שבת, all agree זכור is read that same שבת, not earlier.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the dispute still applies
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with רב הונא and says רב and שמואל argue even when פורים falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the opposite view from רב הונא. He says that even when פורים is on שבת, רב still holds we read זכור one week earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, רב's rule is that remembering must always come before doing, not just on the same day. So even when both fall on שבת, רב moves זכור to the שבת before. שמואל still reads it on the day itself.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
It is still a dispute.
phrases.notes: רב reads early, שמואל does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: עֲדַיִין הִיא מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's claim that everyone agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when פורים is on שבת, רב reads זכור early and שמואל does not.

steps.title: A statement of רב supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A statement passed down in רב's name says that when פורים is on שבת, we read זכור on the שבת before. This matches רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי אבא said that רב said: When פורים falls on שבת, one reads early and reads זכור on the שבת before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רב himself, passed down through two teachers. It shows that רב really does read early even when פורים is on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'איתמר נמי' signal support. רב's own ruling covers exactly the case of פורים on שבת and says to read early. That proves רב נחמן is right: the dispute does still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: the שבת that passed (the previous שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, זכור must always come before פורים, even when פורים itself is on שבת. רב הונא thought everyone agrees here, but רב's own words support רב נחמן.

phrases.english: It was also stated,
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said,
that Rabbi Abba said that Rav said:
When Purim falls on Shabbat —
one reads it early,
reading Zachor on the previous Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's view over רב הונא's.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's claim that רב reads early even when פורים is on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רב passed down by רבי חייא בר אבא through רבי אבא.

steps.title: The third שבת: right after פורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's third reading, פרה אדומה. A ברייתא says the third שבת is the one right after פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: On the third, פרה אדומה. The רבנן taught: Which is the third שבת? The one right after פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the third of the four special readings, פרשת פרה. A ברייתא defines which שבת this is: the שבת right after פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that זכור is settled, the גמרא defines the next reading. The ברייתא ties פרשת פרה to פורים: it comes on the first שבת after it.

keyTerms.meaning: the Red Heifer (פרשת פרה, the third special reading)
right next to פורים, after it

phrases.english: The Mishnah says: On the third, the Red Heifer, etc.
The Sages taught:
Which is the third Shabbat?
Whichever is right after Purim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה after finishing זכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third שבת (פרה) is the שבת right after פורים.

steps.title: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא: the שבת right before ראש חודש ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא defines the third שבת differently: the שבת right before ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: It is the שבת right next to ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second definition of the third שבת that seems to clash with the ברייתא. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will reconcile them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא measures from פורים (the שבת after it). רבי חמא measures from ראש חודש ניסן (the שבת before it). These are not always the same שבת, so it looks like a disagreement.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
The Shabbat right next to (before) Rosh Chodesh Nisan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a definition that seems to conflict with the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third שבת is the one right before ראש חודש ניסן.

steps.title: No real dispute: two different calendar cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two definitions describe different years. רבי חמא speaks of ראש חודש ניסן on שבת, and the ברייתא speaks of ראש חודש ניסן in the middle of the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree. This one is when ראש חודש ניסן falls on שבת; that one is when it falls in the middle of the week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash by showing each source describes a different situation. Both are correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ראש חודש ניסן is on שבת, we read החדש that day, so פרה is the שבת right before it, as רבי חמא says. If ראש חודש ניסן is midweek, החדש is read the שבת before it, and פרה is a week earlier, which is the שבת right after פורים, as the ברייתא says.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שבת' in 'באמצע שבת' means 'week,' not the day of שבת. It means ראש חודש fell on a weekday.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאִיקְּלַע רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: This one (Rabbi Chama) is where Rosh Chodesh Nisan fell on Shabbat,
that one (the Baraita) is where it fell in the middle of the week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent clash between steps 31 and 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different calendar situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רבי חמא give opposing definitions of the third שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are right. Which one applies depends on whether ראש חודש ניסן falls on שבת or midweek.

steps.title: The fourth reading, and ראש חודש אדר on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's fourth reading, החדש. It then brings a ברייתא: when ראש חודש אדר is on שבת, we read כי תשא for שקלים, with the הפטרה about יהוידע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: On the fourth, 'This month shall be for you.' The רבנן taught: When ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת, we read כי תשא, and the הפטרה is the story of יהוידע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the fourth reading and brings a ברייתא that reviews the whole order, starting with the first reading, שקלים. This step gives the Torah reading and הפטרה for שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the readings in order with their הפטרות. For שקלים, the Torah reading is כי תשא, about the half-שקל. The הפטרה is about יהוידע the כהן, who collected money to repair the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This month shall be for you' (פרשת החדש, the fourth reading)
'When you take the count' (the שקלים reading)
יהוידע the כהן (the הפטרה for שקלים)

phrases.english: The Mishnah says: On the fourth, 'This month shall be for you.'
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: When Rosh Chodesh Adar falls on Shabbat —
they read 'When you take the count,'
and the Haftarah is the story of Jehoiada.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the משנה's fourth reading and opens a ברייתא reviewing the order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ראש חודש אדר is on שבת, we read כי תשא with the הפטרה of יהוידע.

steps.title: Which is the first שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines the first שבת (שקלים) as the one whose week contains ראש חודש אדר, even if ראש חודש is on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which is the first שבת? Whichever one has ראש חודש אדר fall within its week, even on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now tells us which שבת counts as the first. It is the שבת tied to the week in which ראש חודש אדר falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ברייתא wording that the גמרא used in Step 17 as a proof for רב: read with 'within it,' a Friday ראש חודש means reading on the שבת before. But in Step 18, שמואל emended the wording to 'on it,' backed by his school's version of the ברייתא. In his version, a Friday ראש חודש means reading on the next day.

phrases.english: And which is the first Shabbat?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁחָל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ,
phrases.english: Whichever one has Rosh Chodesh Adar fall within its week,
even if it falls on Friday.
phrases.notes: רב reads this as moving the reading to the שבת before. שמואל's version reads 'on it' (Step 18).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא by defining the first שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first שבת is the one whose week contains ראש חודש אדר, even if ראש חודש is on Friday.

steps.title: The second שבת: זכור and its הפטרה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the second שבת is זכור, with the הפטרה 'פקדתי.' It is the שבת whose week contains פורים, even if פורים is on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second, זכור, and the הפטרה is 'I remembered.' And which is the second שבת? Whichever one has פורים fall within its week, even on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second reading, זכור, and its הפטרה. It defines the second שבת the same way it defined the first. This definition is the line the גמרא already quoted in step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הפטרה 'פקדתי' is the story of שאול and the war against עמלק, which fits זכור. 'Even on Friday' is the line that seemed to support רב in step 26. שמואל answered in step 27 by reading it 'on it' instead of 'within it.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'I remembered' (the הפטרה for זכור, about שאול and עמלק)

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the four readings is שקלים, זכור, פרה, החדש. The first two are pinned to the weeks of ראש חודש אדר and פורים. פרה is pinned to the שבת after פורים or before ראש חודש ניסן, depending on the calendar. החדש goes with ראש חודש ניסן.

phrases.english: On the second, Zachor,
and the Haftarah is 'I remembered.'
And which is the second Shabbat?
Whichever one has Purim fall within its week,
even if it falls on Friday.
phrases.notes: Same wording discussed in steps 26 and 27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the second reading. Its definition of the second שבת is the same wording used as proof in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second שבת is זכור with the הפטרה 'פקדתי.' It is the שבת whose week contains פורים, even if פורים is on Friday.

steps.title: The third reading is פרה with the הפטרה of וזרקתי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that on the third special שבת we read פרה אדומה, and the הפטרה is 'וזרקתי עליכם' from יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the third שבת we read about the Red Heifer, and the הפטרה is 'And I will sprinkle upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to the third special שבת and names its Torah reading and its הפטרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרשת פרה is about the red heifer that purified people from טומאת מת. The הפטרה in יחזקאל speaks of ה׳ sprinkling pure water on the Jewish people, so it matches the theme of purity.

keyTerms.meaning: The Red Heifer, whose ashes purify people from טומאת מת
'And I will sprinkle upon you' (יחזקאל 36:25), the opening words of the הפטרה

phrases.english: On the third (שבת): the Red Heifer,
and we read as the הפטרה: 'And I will sprinkle upon you.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 36:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the second שבת (זכור) to the third.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Third special שבת: read פרה אדומה; הפטרה 'וזרקתי עליכם'.

steps.title: Which שבת is the third one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines the third special שבת as the one that comes right after פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which is the third שבת? Whichever one comes right after פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us exactly which week פרה is read: the first שבת after פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the ברייתא's own definition of the third שבת, the one רבי חמא ברבי חנינא defined differently in Step 32. Step 33 already explained that both are right, each in a different kind of year.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the ברייתא's own wording, and the גמרא has already settled how it fits with רבי חמא (Step 33).

phrases.english: And which is the third שבת?
Any one that is right next to פורים, after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the timing of the reading named in Step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third special שבת is the first שבת after פורים.

steps.title: The fourth reading is החדש with a הפטרה from יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: On the fourth special שבת we read 'החדש הזה לכם', and the הפטרה is 'כה אמר ה׳ אלהים בראשון באחד לחדש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fourth שבת we read 'This month (shall be for you),' and the הפטרה is 'Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first of the month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the list by naming the fourth special reading and its הפטרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרשת החדש is about making ניסן the first month and preparing the קרבן פסח. The הפטרה in יחזקאל also speaks about the first month, ניסן, so it fits the reading. This completes all four readings from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This month' (שמות 12:2), the opening of פרשת החדש about ניסן
'In the first month, on the first of the month' (יחזקאל 45:18), the הפטרה

steps.whatToRemember: The four special שבתות in order are שקלים, זכור, פרה, and החדש. Each has a matching הפטרה: יהוידע, פקדתי, וזרקתי, and בראשון באחד לחדש.

phrases.english: On the fourth (שבת): 'This month,'
and we read as the הפטרה: 'Thus says the Lord [God]:
In the first month, on the first of the month.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 45:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's list after the third שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fourth special שבת: read החדש הזה; הפטרה 'כה אמר ה׳ אלהים בראשון באחד לחדש'.
